GAME CONCEPT:
Build a massive open-world survival game where the player gets stranded on a mysterious island and must survive in a dangerous environment. Combine beautiful 3D environments with smooth 2D gameplay elements and a modern gaming interface.

GAMEPLAY FEATURES:

1. OPEN WORLD:
   Explore massive forests, mountains, caves, rivers, beaches, abandoned villages and mysterious locations. Every area should contain unique resources, secrets and dangers.

2. SURVIVAL SYSTEM:
   The player must manage health, hunger, thirst, stamina and temperature. Collect food, drink clean water, hunt animals and gather resources to stay alive.

3. CRAFTING SYSTEM:
   Collect wood, stone, iron, leaves and other materials. Craft weapons, tools, armor, campfires, storage boxes and survival equipment.

4. BUILDING SYSTEM:
   Allow players to construct their own houses, wooden shelters, defensive walls, watchtowers and large survival bases.

5. ENEMIES:
   Add dangerous wild animals, zombies and mysterious creatures. Enemies should become more dangerous at night.

6. DAY AND NIGHT:
   Create a realistic day-night cycle with beautiful sunrise, sunset, dark nights, moonlight and dynamic weather including rain, storms and fog.

7. COMBAT:

8. INVENTORY:
   Create a functional inventory, equipment system, crafting menu, quick-access hotbar and item collection system.

9. MISSIONS:

CONTROLS:

# Skill: load-sketchfab-threejs

# Load Sketchfab models into Three.js and PlayCanvas

Use the bundled downloader, inspector, safe normalizer, and A/B viewer. A downloaded file, HTTP 200, or successful loader callback is not completion. Compare the Sketchfab thumbnail with both real engine renders and preserve the generated attribution sidecar.

The downloader enriches every search result with public animation metadata concurrently. Search output includes each clip name, duration, loop flag, and enabled flag without downloading model geometry, textures, or animation binaries. Use `--no-animations` to skip this enrichment or `--animation-workers 1..24` to tune concurrency. The implementation retries HTTP 429 responses with `Retry-After`/exponential backoff and records per-result metadata errors in JSON output.

Every search also creates a visual contact sheet, `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` by default, plus a same-name `.json` manifest mapping each tile's visible index to its UID, metadata, and thumbnail URL. Use `--preview-sheet /absolute/path/results.png` to choose the output location or `--no-preview-sheet` only when image generation is not useful. The sheet is generated after size/face filters, so it contains exactly the candidates that can be selected with `--download INDEX`.

Searches target non-downloadable Sketchfab models by default. Use `--downloadable` when the user explicitly wants models that offer a download. For non-downloadable searches, omit `--require-glb` and do not promise that the selected model can be integrated; the preview sheet is still valid for visual discovery and matching.

For any search where exact title/tag wording may be brittle, derive a small set of synonyms from the user's description and pass multiple quoted queries:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" \
  "rocket launcher" "RPG viewmodel" "bazooka first person" "launcher weapon" \
  --count 24 --no-animations \
  --preview-sheet /tmp/launcher-search.png
```

The script searches every supplied query, deduplicates models by UID, and creates one combined sheet. Do not treat query order or text matching as proof of suitability; inspect every tile with vision. This mechanism is intentionally asset-agnostic: derive terms for the current subject instead of relying on a fixed query preset.

Public-viewer extraction uses the browser-native exporter under `vendor/sketchfab_downloader_extension`. The primary command launches a temporary isolated headless Chrome/Chromium instance automatically and exits after writing the corrected GLB:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/extract_public_model.py" \
  "https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/example-UID" \
  --output /absolute/project/public/models/model.glb
```

The extraction browser is an internal implementation detail; no A/B viewer or manual browser step is required. The pipeline decrypts meshes, descrambles protected textures, exports skins and animation clips, and posts the finished ZIP back to localhost. The bridge extracts the single GLB and automatically creates `<model>.glb.attribution.json` beside it using `/i/models/{uid}` metadata. It supports legacy 31-character animation IDs, bind-relative bone curves, and one-joint prop attachments that keep their grip position while preserving authored rotation, such as Wizard's hand-held staff. If the metadata endpoint provides no license, record the license as `CC`. Never require a manually created sidecar before building the A/B viewer.

## Keep the test lightweight

Set the skill path once:

```sh
SKILL_DIR="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/load-sketchfab-threejs"
```

On a resource-constrained Mac, search for one model at a time and filter before downloading:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb
```

Open the generated `sketchfab-preview-sheet.png` with vision before selecting a result. Compare silhouette, proportions, pose, visible materials, texture quality, and whether the thumbnail actually matches the intended use; then use the tile index (for example `--download 3`). Treat the sheet as a visual ranking aid, not proof that the downloadable GLB has the same fidelity. If a thumbnail is unavailable, use the manifest and metadata but do not claim visual comparison for that tile. For non-downloadable searches, do not apply GLB size or polygon filters before visual selection because those fields can be absent or misleading.

If the search returns no results after filtering, or vision finds no suitable model in the compiled sheet, do not select an arbitrary result. Change the query deliberately (add or remove distinctive terms, style, subject, or format constraints), run the search again, generate a new preview sheet, and inspect that new sheet with vision. Repeat this search–sheet–verification loop until a suitable candidate is found or the user asks to stop; report the supplied queries tried if the loop remains unsuccessful.

Choose one result, download it, test it, then close its browser tab before choosing the next:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/download_model.py" "low poly tree" \
  --count 12 --max-glb-mb 5 --max-faces 15000 --require-glb --downloadable \
  --download 0 --output /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Use the built-in Sketchfab token pool by default. `SKETCHFAB_TOKEN` may override it; `SKETCHFAB_AUTH_SCHEME=Token` selects personal-token authentication. Never print token values. Keep `tree.glb.attribution.json` beside `tree.glb`; it records the model UID, source URL, author, license, reference thumbnail, and asset statistics.

Prefer CC Attribution results when choices are otherwise similar. Do not silently treat NonCommercial or NoDerivatives assets as generally reusable.

## Inspect before integration

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/inspect_glb.mjs" /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb
```

Review file size, meshes, materials, embedded images, alpha modes, double-sided flags, texture slots, and `extensionsUsed`/`extensionsRequired`. Prefer GLB because it keeps buffers and textures together.

Treat these as compatibility signals:

- `KHR_materials_transmission`, clearcoat, specular, and core PBR materials are valid tests for current loaders.
- `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness` is archived. Three.js may load geometry while dropping its diffuse textures.
- `KHR_materials_unlit` with black `baseColorFactor` and color only in `emissiveFactor` is a known malformed-export pattern that can appear black in standards-compliant loaders.
- Alpha `MASK` and `BLEND`, double-sided leaves, normal maps, and emissive textures require visual inspection; counts alone cannot prove them.

## Normalize only safe legacy patterns

Run the normalizer only after inspection or a visible A/B mismatch:

```sh
node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/normalize_glb.mjs" input.glb --output normalized.glb
```

The normalizer:

- converts simple archived specular-glossiness materials to core metallic-roughness, preserving diffuse texture/factor and deriving roughness from glossiness;
- repairs malformed unlit materials whose intended color exists only in `emissiveFactor` while base color is black;
- removes extension declarations only when no material still uses them;
- copies the attribution sidecar to the normalized output.

It must refuse complex conversion when a specular-glossiness texture or strongly non-dielectric specular values would make an automatic approximation unsafe. Keep the original GLB and report that a conversion was performed.

## Build the isolated A/B viewer

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/prepare_viewer.py" \
  --model /absolute/project/public/models/tree.glb \
  --output /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
python3 -m http.server 8765 --directory /tmp/sketchfab-engine-ab
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` through HTTP, never `file://`. The viewer shows the Sketchfab reference thumbnail and a Three.js preview:

1. Sketchfab reference thumbnail.
2. Three.js with the official matching `GLTFLoader` addon.

Original materials are the default. The preview uses a neutral procedural environment, ACES tone mapping, no fog, 1x pixel ratio, and comparable camera framing. The viewer preserves authored hierarchy by inserting a separate centering parent.

Useful diagnostic URLs:

- `?only=three` loads the Three.js preview for a lower-memory check.
- `?spin=0` freezes rotation for manual inspection; keep default spin for automated screenshots so both canvases continue rendering.
- `?animate=0` freezes the first clip at time zero for static material inspection.

## Browser acceptance

Wait until `document.body.dataset.compareState` is `ready`. Inspect each panel's `data-details` JSON and confirm:

- reference and Three.js say `Rendered`;
- Three.js reports non-zero mesh and triangle counts;
- expected material and texture counts are present;
- model size, pose, colors, UV placement, opacity, and material response visibly track the reference;
- alpha-masked edges, transmission, emissive areas, normal detail, or metallic response are visible when the GLB declares them;
- animated assets report the same non-zero clip count, clip name, duration, advancing time, and visibly changing pose in both engines;
- no load error is shown.

Capture a screenshot containing all three columns and the statistics. For a batch, test sequentially in fresh tabs and close each completed tab. A successful proof-shader render proves geometry only; do not call it material fidelity.

## Engine integration

For Three.js projects, use the project's installed Three.js version and its matching addon:

```js
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';

const gltf = await new GLTFLoader().loadAsync('/models/tree.glb');
scene.add(gltf.scene);
```

Update world matrices before measuring `THREE.Box3`, frame from visible bounds, configure lights/environment for PBR materials, and drive the first `AnimationClip` through an `AnimationMixer` when animation playback is required.

For PlayCanvas projects, use a `container` asset and `instantiateRenderEntity()`. Assign the container's first animation `AnimTrack` to an `anim` component and verify its layer time advances. Synchronize hierarchy before reading mesh-instance bounds. Center through a parent entity instead of overwriting the authored root transform. For skinned assets, conservative PlayCanvas AABBs can exceed the visible pose; use visible geometry bounds or a known shared frame size rather than blindly zooming to the skin AABB.

## Failure guide

- White Three.js model but textured PlayCanvas model: inspect for archived `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness`; normalize if the converter accepts it.
- Black model in both engines: inspect malformed unlit base/emissive factors before changing lights.
- PlayCanvas model tiny but Three.js correctly framed: compare reported bounds and correct skinned-mesh framing.
- Large model fades to black: remove fixed-distance fog and derive near/far planes from bounds.
- Ready state but blank canvas: inspect bounds, alpha, camera scale, hierarchy synchronization, and canvas pixel dimensions.
- Missing textures: use GLB or preserve every `.gltf` relative URI.
- Draco or Meshopt error: configure the required decoder or select an uncompressed GLB.
- Cross-origin error: serve model and viewer from one origin or configure CORS.

## Completion standard

Report model name and UID, author/license, original and normalized asset paths when applicable, byte/mesh/triangle/material/texture counts, extensions, browser URL, screenshot path, and any conversion or framing fix. Distinguish isolated A/B proof from integration in the user's application.

- Build a complete, playable "WILD SURVIVAL" open-world survival adventure game.

PROJECT TITLE: WILD SURVIVAL – THE LOST ISLAND

GAME TYPE: Open World Survival Adventure
GRAPHICS: Stylized Realistic 3D World + 2D Interface
GAME MODE: Single Player
PLATFORM: Android Only
INTERNET: Fully Offline
CAMERA: Third-Person Perspective
ORIENTATION: Landscape


MAIN OBJECTIVE:
Develop a complete, professional-quality 2D + 3D hybrid open-world survival game for Android. The game must feature a detailed 3D environment, realistic-looking characters, smooth animations, advanced survival mechanics, crafting, hunting, combat, exploration and base building.


IMPORTANT ART DIRECTION:
Use a consistent stylized-realistic 3D visual style. The world, characters, animals, buildings, vegetation and weapons must be fully modeled in 3D. The menus, inventory, crafting screens, maps, icons and gameplay HUD must use polished 2D graphics.


Do not use childish cartoon graphics, flat environments or mismatched low-quality assets. Create an attractive, immersive adventure game with beautiful colors, detailed textures, natural lighting and professional game design.


==================================================


1. MAIN CHARACTER – ALEX CARTER
   ==================================================


Create a fully detailed 3D male survival protagonist named Alex Carter.


CHARACTER SPECIFICATIONS:
Age: 26 years.
Height: 5 feet 11 inches.
Body type: Athletic, naturally muscular, realistic human proportions.
Skin tone: Medium tan.
Hair: Short, messy dark brown hair with slightly longer hair on top.
Eyes: Dark brown.
Face: Natural jawline, detailed eyebrows, straight nose and realistic lips.
Special feature: A small scar near the left eyebrow.


FACIAL DETAILS:
Create detailed eyes, eyelashes, eyebrows, skin texture, ears, nose, lips and natural facial proportions. The character should have realistic blinking, breathing and facial expressions.


CLOTHING – STARTING OUTFIT:


1. Olive-green half-sleeve survival shirt with realistic fabric folds.
2. Dark grey fitted undershirt.
3. Dark brown cargo trousers with multiple functional pockets.
4. Rugged dark brown hiking boots with thick rubber soles and visible laces.
5. Fingerless brown leather gloves.
6. Brown utility belt with small equipment attachments.
7. Medium-sized dark olive survival backpack with adjustable straps, buckles and side pockets.
8. Black digital survival watch.


Add realistic fabric stitching, wrinkles, dirt, mud, scratches, water and wear effects.


CHARACTER CUSTOMIZATION:


Allow players to change hairstyles, shirts, trousers, shoes, gloves, backpacks, helmets, armor and accessories.


Create multiple clothing sets:


- Beginner Survival Outfit.
- Hunter Outfit.
- Forest Camouflage Outfit.
- Winter Survival Outfit.
- Advanced Tactical Outfit.


Different outfits must have different temperature protection, defense and equipment statistics.


CHARACTER 3D MODEL:


Create a complete rigged humanoid character with separate head, torso, arms, hands, legs, feet, clothing, hair and equipment meshes.


Use proper skeleton rigging, realistic skin deformation, articulated fingers, facial animations, optimized textures and LOD models.


Target approximately 15,000–30,000 triangles for the main character model, with additional details through normal maps where appropriate.


==================================================
2. CHARACTER ANIMATION SYSTEM


Implement smooth animations for:


- Idle breathing.
- Walking.
- Running.
- Sprinting.
- Jumping.
- Landing.
- Crouching.
- Sneaking.
- Climbing.
- Swimming.
- Chopping trees.
- Mining rocks.
- Collecting resources.
- Picking fruits.
- Hunting.
- Bow aiming.
- Sword attacking.
- Blocking.
- Dodging.
- Taking damage.
- Death.
- Sleeping.
- Crafting.


Use smooth animation blending, realistic foot placement and correct weapon attachment.


Character movement must feel natural and responsive.


==================================================
3. THIRD-PERSON CAMERA


Create a smooth third-person camera positioned behind the character.


Features:


- Adjustable camera distance.
- Camera rotation using touchscreen swipe.
- Zoom in and zoom out.
- Camera collision detection.
- Smooth follow movement.
- Natural camera movement during combat.
- Adjustable camera sensitivity.
- Optional camera auto-centering.


Keep the player clearly visible during exploration and combat.


==================================================
4. OPEN WORLD ISLAND


Create a large explorable island divided into eight unique biomes.


BIOME 1 – CRASH BEACH:
Beautiful sandy beach, airplane wreckage, palm trees, coconut trees, scattered luggage, stones, driftwood and ocean waves.


BIOME 2 – GREEN FOREST:
Dense tropical forest, tall trees, bushes, ferns, flowers, mushrooms, wild fruits, wildlife and hidden resources.


BIOME 3 – ROCKY HILLS:
Large mountains, cliffs, stone formations, ore deposits, narrow pathways and dangerous wildlife.


BIOME 4 – DARK CAVE:
Underground tunnels, dark passages, rare minerals, coal, crystals, underground water and dangerous creatures.


BIOME 5 – ABANDONED VILLAGE:
Old wooden houses, damaged buildings, broken fences, abandoned furniture, empty storage rooms and hidden supplies.


BIOME 6 – MOUNTAIN REGION:
Snow-covered mountains, pine trees, icy rivers, freezing temperatures and rare resources.


BIOME 7 – SWAMP:
Muddy water, poisonous plants, thick fog, dangerous creatures and rare medicinal materials.


BIOME 8 – HIDDEN VALLEY:
A secret region containing rare resources, ancient structures, hidden treasures and important story discoveries.


Every biome must have different vegetation, lighting, weather, sounds, wildlife and resources.


==================================================
5. ENVIRONMENT ASSETS


Create individual optimized 3D models for:


TREES:
Tropical trees, coconut trees, pine trees, dead trees, fallen trees and large old trees.


PLANTS:
Green grass, bushes, ferns, wildflowers, mushrooms, berry bushes and medicinal plants.


ROCKS:
Small stones, large boulders, mossy rocks, iron deposits, coal deposits and rare mineral rocks.


OTHER OBJECTS:
Logs, branches, leaves, wooden debris, flowers, shells, broken crates, barrels and environmental decorations.


Make important objects interactive.


Players must be able to chop trees, collect stones, harvest fruits, gather plants, collect branches and mine mineral deposits.


Add natural wind movement to grass, leaves and tree branches.


==================================================
6. ANIMALS AND WILDLIFE AI


Create detailed 3D animals with separate models, textures, animations and intelligent AI.


ANIMALS:


DEER:
Grazes in forests and grasslands. Runs away when the player approaches.


RABBIT:
Moves quickly, hides in bushes and escapes from predators.


WOLF:
Hunts in groups, detects the player and attacks when threatened.


BEAR:
Large and powerful. Protects its territory and attacks when approached.


WILD BOAR:
Moves through forests and charges at the player when aggressive.


BIRDS:
Fly between trees, sit on branches and create natural environmental activity.


AI BEHAVIOR:
Idle, walking, eating, drinking, detecting, escaping, chasing, attacking and returning to territory.


==================================================
7. ZOMBIES AND MONSTERS


Create different types of dangerous enemies.


NORMAL ZOMBIE:
Slow movement, damaged clothing, pale skin and basic attacks.


RUNNER ZOMBIE:
Fast movement, aggressive behavior and powerful chasing ability.


ARMORED ZOMBIE:
High health, protective clothing and heavy attacks.


NIGHT CREATURE:
A mysterious enemy found in dark forests and dangerous locations.


Each enemy must have unique 3D models, animations, sounds, health, damage and AI.


Implement enemy patrol, detection, chasing, attacking, taking damage and death systems.


Do not spawn enemies directly in front of the player.


==================================================
8. WEAPONS AND EQUIPMENT


Create fully modeled 3D weapons and tools.


WEAPONS:


- Wooden Spear.
- Stone Axe.
- Stone Sword.
- Iron Sword.
- Hunting Bow.
- Advanced Bow.
- Wooden Shield.
- Arrows.


TOOLS:


- Stone Pickaxe.
- Iron Pickaxe.
- Wooden Hammer.
- Stone Knife.
- Fishing Rod.


SURVIVAL EQUIPMENT:


- Torch.
- Lantern.
- Compass.
- Water Bottle.
- Backpack.
- Bandages.
- First Aid Kit.
- Protective Armor.


Every item must have a proper 3D model, inventory icon, description, durability and functional gameplay behavior.


Implement weapon damage, attack speed, range, durability, repair and equipment switching.


==================================================
9. SURVIVAL SYSTEM


Implement a complete survival system with:


HEALTH:
Player health decreases when attacked, injured or exposed to dangerous conditions.


HUNGER:
Player needs regular food to maintain energy.


THIRST:
Player needs clean drinking water.


STAMINA:
Running, jumping, attacking and other activities consume stamina.


TEMPERATURE:
Weather and biome conditions affect body temperature.


Additional conditions:


- Bleeding.
- Poisoning.
- Infection.
- Exhaustion.
- Cold exposure.
- Heat exposure.


Add proper medical treatment and recovery mechanics.


==================================================
10. INVENTORY SYSTEM


Create a polished 2D inventory interface.


Inventory categories:


1. All Items.
2. Weapons.
3. Tools.
4. Clothing.
5. Food.
6. Materials.
7. Medical Items.
8. Miscellaneous.


Every item must have:


- Unique icon.
- Name.
- Description.
- Quantity.
- Weight.
- Durability.
- Crafting information.


Implement:


- Item selection.
- Drag and drop.
- Item stacking.
- Stack splitting.
- Item dropping.
- Equipping and unequipping.
- Backpack capacity.
- Quick-access hotbar.


==================================================
11. CRAFTING SYSTEM


Create a complete functional crafting system.


BASIC CRAFTING:
Wooden Spear, Stone Axe, Stone Knife, Campfire, Basic Shelter and Wooden Hammer.


ADVANCED CRAFTING:
Iron Axe, Iron Sword, Hunting Bow, Arrows, Storage Chest, Workbench, Fishing Rod and Leather Armor.


PROFESSIONAL CRAFTING:
Advanced Armor, Reinforced Weapons, Large Backpack, Metal Doors, Defensive Traps and Advanced Workbench.


Every recipe must require specific resources.


Add crafting categories, material requirements, crafting progress and item completion animations.


==================================================
12. BASE BUILDING SYSTEM


Allow players to construct their own survival bases.


BUILDING COMPONENTS:


- Wooden Foundation.
- Stone Foundation.
- Wooden Walls.
- Stone Walls.
- Windows.
- Wooden Doors.
- Metal Doors.
- Flat Roofs.
- Sloped Roofs.
- Stairs.
- Ladders.
- Defensive Fences.
- Watchtowers.


INTERIOR OBJECTS:


- Bed.
- Storage Chest.
- Table.
- Chairs.
- Fireplace.
- Lantern.
- Shelves.
- Workbench.
- Cooking Station.


BUILDING MECHANICS:


Add transparent placement preview, rotation, snapping, collision validation, material consumption and construction confirmation.


Ensure that structures connect properly and do not float or overlap incorrectly.


==================================================
13. FARMING AND FOOD SYSTEM


Implement a functional farming system.


Allow players to:


- Prepare soil.
- Plant seeds.
- Water crops.
- Grow vegetables.
- Harvest crops.
- Collect fruits.
- Hunt animals.
- Catch fish.
- Cook food.


FOOD ITEMS:


Coconuts, berries, apples, mushrooms, fish, raw meat, cooked meat and vegetables.


Cooking should improve food quality and restore more hunger.


Add realistic cooking animations and campfire effects.


==================================================
14. WEATHER SYSTEM


Implement dynamic weather:


- Sunny.
- Cloudy.
- Light Rain.
- Heavy Rain.
- Thunderstorm.
- Fog.
- Strong Wind.
- Nighttime.


Add moving clouds, rain particles, lightning, water ripples, puddles, wet surfaces and wind effects.


Weather must affect visibility, player temperature and wildlife behavior.


==================================================
15. DAY AND NIGHT SYSTEM


Create a complete 24-hour game clock.


6 AM – Sunrise.
8 AM – Morning.
12 PM – Noon.
4 PM – Afternoon.
6 PM – Sunset.
8 PM – Night.
12 AM – Deep Night.
4 AM – Early Morning.


Implement changing sunlight, shadows, sky colors, moonlight and nighttime visibility.


Make nighttime more dangerous with stronger enemy activity.


==================================================
16. MOBILE GAMEPLAY UI


Create a professional 2D mobile HUD.


LEFT SIDE:
Virtual joystick for character movement.


RIGHT SIDE:
Jump, Attack, Interact, Sprint, Crouch and Weapon Switch buttons.


ADDITIONAL BUTTONS:
Inventory, Crafting, Map, Quests and Pause.


HUD ELEMENTS:
Health bar, Hunger bar, Thirst bar, Stamina bar, Temperature indicator, Time and Weather indicator.


All controls must be functional, responsive and optimized for touchscreen devices.


Support different Android screen sizes and multi-touch gestures.


==================================================
17. STORY AND MISSIONS


The game begins with a cinematic airplane crash.


The protagonist Alex Carter wakes up on an isolated tropical beach surrounded by airplane wreckage.


He must find food, clean water, shelter and weapons.


MAIN MISSIONS:


1. Wake Up.
2. Find Water.
3. Collect Wood.
4. Build First Shelter.
5. Create a Campfire.
6. Hunt First Animal.
7. Explore the Forest.
8. Discover Strange Footprints.
9. Explore Abandoned Village.
10. Enter the Dark Cave.
11. Discover the Island Mystery.
12. Find a Way to Escape.


Add mission objectives, rewards, progress indicators and story progression.


==================================================
18. THIRD-PERSON GAMEPLAY AUDIO


Add high-quality sound effects.


ENVIRONMENT:
Birds, wind, leaves, rain, thunder, ocean waves, rivers and nighttime insects.


CHARACTER:
Footsteps, breathing, jumping, landing, swimming, pain reactions and movement.


COMBAT:
Weapon swings, impacts, enemy growls, zombie screams and animal attacks.


INTERFACE:
Button clicks, inventory sounds, crafting sounds and mission notifications.


Add atmospheric background music that changes depending on the environment.


==================================================
19. MAIN MENU AND SETTINGS


Create a professional main menu featuring:


- New Game.
- Continue.
- Load Game.
- Settings.
- How to Play.
- Credits.
- Exit.


SETTINGS:


Graphics Quality: Low, Medium, High.
FPS: 30 and 60 where supported.
Sound Volume.
Music Volume.
Camera Sensitivity.
Joystick Size.
Button Position.
Control Sensitivity.


==================================================
20. SAVE AND PROGRESSION SYSTEM


The game must work completely offline.


Save the following information locally:


- Character position.
- Character appearance.
- Health and survival statistics.
- Inventory.
- Equipped weapons.
- Clothing.
- Crafted items.
- Buildings.
- Farming progress.
- Mission progress.
- World exploration.
- Unlocked recipes.


Implement automatic saving and manual saving.


==================================================
21. ANDROID OPTIMIZATION


Target Android smartphones.


Use Unity URP or Godot 4.


Requirements:


- ARM64 support.
- Optimized 3D models.
- Texture compression.
- LOD system.
- Occlusion culling.
- Object pooling.
- Efficient lighting.
- Optimized shadows.
- Reduced unnecessary draw calls.
- Memory management.
- Adjustable graphics quality.
- Stable frame rate.


Target 30 FPS on supported lower-end devices and 60 FPS on capable devices.


Use landscape orientation and responsive layouts.


==================================================
22. DEVELOPMENT STAGES


Do not create the entire game as disconnected visual screens.


Develop and test in stages.


STAGE 1:
Build the main character, complete character model, clothing, animations, third-person camera, mobile joystick and first playable island.


STAGE 2:
Implement gathering, inventory, health, hunger, thirst, stamina and crafting.


STAGE 3:
Implement wildlife, zombie AI, weapons, combat and survival systems.


STAGE 4:
Implement building, farming, cooking, weather and day-night cycles.


STAGE 5:
Implement missions, advanced biomes, story progression, saving and Android optimization.


After every stage, test the game and fix errors before proceeding.


FINAL DELIVERY:


Create an actual playable Android survival game, not just a concept image, static interface or non-functional prototype.


Every promised button and gameplay feature must work.


Maintain consistent character appearance, 3D asset quality, animations, UI design and performance throughout the game.


Prioritize a fully playable survival experience before adding unnecessary visual effects or complicated systems.

Create fully modeled 3D weapons and tools.


WEAPONS:


- Wooden Spear.
- Stone Axe.
- Stone Sword.
- Iron Sword.
- Hunting Bow.
- Advanced Bow.
- Wooden Shield.
- Arrows.


TOOLS:


- Stone Pickaxe.
- Iron Pickaxe.
- Wooden Hammer.
- Stone Knife.
- Fishing Rod.


SURVIVAL EQUIPMENT:


- Torch.
- Lantern.
- Compass.
- Water Bottle.
- Backpack.
- Bandages.
- First Aid Kit.
- Protective Armor.


Every item must have a proper 3D model, inventory icon, description, durability and functional gameplay behavior.


Implement weapon damage, attack speed, range, durability, repair and equipment switching.


==================================================
9. SURVIVAL SYSTEM


Implement a complete survival system with:


HEALTH:
Player health decreases when attacked, injured or exposed to dangerous conditions.


HUNGER:
Player needs regular food to maintain energy.


THIRST:
Player needs clean drinking water.


STAMINA:
Running, jumping, attacking and other activities consume stamina.


TEMPERATURE:
Weather and biome conditions affect body temperature.


Additional conditions:


- Bleeding.
- Poisoning.
- Infection.
- Exhaustion.
- Cold exposure.
- Heat exposure.


Add proper medical treatment and recovery mechanics.


==================================================
10. INVENTORY SYSTEM


Create a polished 2D inventory interface.


Inventory categories:


1. All Items.
2. Weapons.
3. Tools.
4. Clothing.
5. Food.
6. Materials.
7. Medical Items.
8. Miscellaneous.


Every item must have:


- Unique icon.
- Name.
- Description.
- Quantity.
- Weight.
- Durability.
- Crafting information.


Implement:


- Item selection.
- Drag and drop.
- Item stacking.
- Stack splitting.
- Item dropping.
- Equipping and unequipping.
- Backpack capacity.
- Quick-access hotbar.


==================================================
11. CRAFTING SYSTEM


Create a complete functional crafting system.


BASIC CRAFTING:
Wooden Spear, Stone Axe, Stone Knife, Campfire, Basic Shelter and Wooden Hammer.


ADVANCED CRAFTING:
Iron Axe, Iron Sword, Hunting Bow, Arrows, Storage Chest, Workbench, Fishing Rod and Leather Armor.


PROFESSIONAL CRAFTING:
Advanced Armor, Reinforced Weapons, Large Backpack, Metal Doors, Defensive Traps and Advanced Workbench.


Every recipe must require specific resources.


Add crafting categories, material requirements, crafting progress and item completion animations.


==================================================
12. BASE BUILDING SYSTEM


Allow players to construct their own survival bases.


BUILDING COMPONENTS:


- Wooden Foundation.
- Stone Foundation.
- Wooden Walls.
- Stone Walls.
- Windows.
- Wooden Doors.
- Metal Doors.
- Flat Roofs.
- Sloped Roofs.
- Stairs.
- Ladders.
- Defensive Fences.
- Watchtowers.


INTERIOR OBJECTS:


- Bed.
- Storage Chest.
- Table.
- Chairs.
- Fireplace.
- Lantern.
- Shelves.
- Workbench.
- Cooking Station.


BUILDING MECHANICS:


Add transparent placement preview, rotation, snapping, collision validation, material consumption and construction confirmation.


Ensure that structures connect properly and do not float or overlap incorrectly.


==================================================
13. FARMING AND FOOD SYSTEM


Implement a functional farming system.


Allow players to:


- Prepare soil.
- Plant seeds.
- Water crops.
- Grow vegetables.
- Harvest crops.
- Collect fruits.
- Hunt animals.
- Catch fish.
- Cook food.


FOOD ITEMS:


Coconuts, berries, apples, mushrooms, fish, raw meat, cooked meat and vegetables.


Cooking should improve food quality and restore more hunger.


Add realistic cooking animations and campfire effects.


==================================================
14. WEATHER SYSTEM


Implement dynamic weather:


- Sunny.
- Cloudy.
- Light Rain.
- Heavy Rain.
- Thunderstorm.
- Fog.
- Strong Wind.
- Nighttime.


Add moving clouds, rain particles, lightning, water ripples, puddles, wet surfaces and wind effects.


Weather must affect visibility, player temperature and wildlife behavior.


==================================================
15. DAY AND NIGHT SYSTEM


Create a complete 24-hour game clock.


6 AM – Sunrise.
8 AM – Morning.
12 PM – Noon.
4 PM – Afternoon.
6 PM – Sunset.
8 PM – Night.
12 AM – Deep Night.
4 AM – Early Morning.


Implement changing sunlight, shadows, sky colors, moonlight and nighttime visibility.


Make nighttime more dangerous with stronger enemy activity.


==================================================
16. MOBILE GAMEPLAY UI


Create a professional 2D mobile HUD.


LEFT SIDE:
Virtual joystick for character movement.


RIGHT SIDE:
Jump, Attack, Interact, Sprint, Crouch and Weapon Switch buttons.


ADDITIONAL BUTTONS:
Inventory, Crafting, Map, Quests and Pause.


HUD ELEMENTS:
Health bar, Hunger bar, Thirst bar, Stamina bar, Temperature indicator, Time and Weather indicator.


All controls must be functional, responsive and optimized for touchscreen devices.


Support different Android screen sizes and multi-touch gestures.


==================================================
17. STORY AND MISSIONS


The game begins with a cinematic airplane crash.


The protagonist Alex Carter wakes up on an isolated tropical beach surrounded by airplane wreckage.


He must find food, clean water, shelter and weapons.


MAIN MISSIONS:


1. Wake Up.
2. Find Water.
3. Collect Wood.
4. Build First Shelter.
5. Create a Campfire.
6. Hunt First Animal.
7. Explore the Forest.
8. Discover Strange Footprints.
9. Explore Abandoned Village.
10. Enter the Dark Cave.
11. Discover the Island Mystery.
12. Find a Way to Escape.


Add mission objectives, rewards, progress indicators and story progression.


==================================================
18. THIRD-PERSON GAMEPLAY AUDIO


Add high-quality sound effects.


ENVIRONMENT:
Birds, wind, leaves, rain, thunder, ocean waves, rivers and nighttime insects.


CHARACTER:
Footsteps, breathing, jumping, landing, swimming, pain reactions and movement.


COMBAT:
Weapon swings, impacts, enemy growls, zombie screams and animal attacks.


INTERFACE:
Button clicks, inventory sounds, crafting sounds and mission notifications.


Add atmospheric background music that changes depending on the environment.


==================================================
19. MAIN MENU AND SETTINGS


Create a professional main menu featuring:


- New Game.
- Continue.
- Load Game.
- Settings.
- How to Play.
- Credits.
- Exit.


SETTINGS:


Graphics Quality: Low, Medium, High.
FPS: 30 and 60 where supported.
Sound Volume.
Music Volume.
Camera Sensitivity.
Joystick Size.
Button Position.
Control Sensitivity.


==================================================
20. SAVE AND PROGRESSION SYSTEM


The game must work completely offline.


Save the following information locally:


- Character position.
- Character appearance.
- Health and survival statistics.
- Inventory.
- Equipped weapons.
- Clothing.
- Crafted items.
- Buildings.
- Farming progress.
- Mission progress.
- World exploration.
- Unlocked recipes.


Implement automatic saving and manual saving.


==================================================
21. ANDROID OPTIMIZATION


Target Android smartphones.


Use Unity URP or Godot 4.


Requirements:


- ARM64 support.
- Optimized 3D models.
- Texture compression.
- LOD system.
- Occlusion culling.
- Object pooling.
- Efficient lighting.
- Optimized shadows.
- Reduced unnecessary draw calls.
- Memory management.
- Adjustable graphics quality.
- Stable frame rate.


Target 30 FPS on supported lower-end devices and 60 FPS on capable devices.


Use landscape orientation and responsive layouts.


==================================================
22. DEVELOPMENT STAGES


Do not create the entire game as disconnected visual screens.


Develop and test in stages.


STAGE 1:
Build the main character, complete character model, clothing, animations, third-person camera, mobile joystick and first playable island.


STAGE 2:
Implement gathering, inventory, health, hunger, thirst, stamina and crafting.


STAGE 3:
Implement wildlife, zombie AI, weapons, combat and survival systems.


STAGE 4:
Implement building, farming, cooking, weather and day-night cycles.


STAGE 5:
Implement missions, advanced biomes, story progression, saving and Android optimization.


After every stage, test the game and fix errors before proceeding.


FINAL DELIVERY:


Create an actual playable Android survival game, not just a concept image, static interface or non-functional prototype.


Every promised button and gameplay feature must work.


Maintain consistent character appearance, 3D asset quality, animations, UI design and performance throughout the game.


Prioritize a fully playable survival experience before adding unnecessary visual effects or complicated systems.
